_doc: Live hypothesis queue for the autonomous campaign. Owned by the planner/ideator; statuses flipped by the cycle. Seeded 2026-08-09 from experiments/roadmap.md (prior-evidence column), findings.md, diagnosis.md Q01/Q02 and Vahidi 2025 (arXiv:2506.13799). Ranked by expected value / cost. The ideator extends this file; it must dedup against autoresearch/killed.json first.

items.title: HARDWARE RE-BASELINE — re-measure the champions on this machine before any cycle
items.hypothesis: Not a hypothesis — a prerequisite. Every number in sota.json was measured on Apple MPS. Scores and noise floors are hardware-dependent (different kernels, different non-determinism), so on any new device the champions and their sigmas must be re-measured before a single variant is judged.
items.rationale: The whole Phase-7 verdict rule compares a variant to the champion. Comparing a CUDA-measured variant against an MPS-measured champion is exactly the moving-comparator error the auditor exists to catch — except the auditor cannot see it, because the device is not part of config_hash. The deterministic scorer-parity test (tests/test_metrics.py, 34,751,902) is what carries over between machines; training trajectories do not.
items.method: 1) pytest tests/ -q must be fully green (the scorer parity is the portability anchor). 2) Run the current champions at the screen seeds on all three datasets: H35 on connectome/mouse, H30 on microns/mouse, role=implement. 3) Recompute mean/std per dataset with autoresearch/audit.py. 4) If any champion mean or sigma differs materially from sota.json, update sota.json via update_sota.py --force with the hardware change logged in experiments/log.md, and update the screen_delta_pp values in campaign.yaml to 2x the NEW sigma. 5) Record the device name and torch version in the log entry.
items.kill_condition: Not killable — it is a gate. If the scorer parity test fails on the new machine, STOP: the environment is wrong and no result from it is admissible.
items.est_cost: cheap-medium (about 9 runs; connectome ~4 min each, microns ~12 min each on MPS — faster on a discrete GPU)
items.expected_pp: n/a — this establishes the reference frame, it does not move the metric

items.title: SCC-decomposed recursive bounded-span insertion (the Vahidi route)
items.hypothesis: Condensing the graph into SCCs, ordering the condensation DAG topologically, and then recursively applying exact-gain insertion WITHIN the giant SCC (rather than over the whole line) recovers a large part of the remaining 0.70 pp to the 84.6147% reference, at bounded cost.
items.rationale: Vahidi 2025 reaches 84.61% on this exact graph with cheap greedy + bounded-span insertion + SCC and NO MIP, so the residual is demonstrably reachable by combinatorial means. Our H22 kill only falsified RANK-window locality (killed.json M4); a structural (SCC) neighbourhood is a different object. dr_tmp/FINDINGS_underrelaxation.md E2 warns that a ONE-SHOT SCC split recovers ~nothing (inter-SCC edges 1.50%, giant SCC 92.82%) — so the hypothesis is specifically the RECURSIVE within-giant-SCC form.
items.kill_condition: If recursive within-SCC insertion on the giant SCC does not beat the champion sift on the prototype proxy, the decomposition story is dead and we stop paying for SCC machinery.
items.est_cost: medium (SCC via scipy.csgraph is cheap; the recursion is the work)
items.expected_pp: connectome: up to +0.7 (the whole residual) if the Vahidi mechanism transfers; honest estimate +0.1 to +0.4

items.title: Cycle-triggered under-relaxation (fix the microns regression, make H35 a general win)
items.hypothesis: Switching from Jacobi (alpha=1) to under-relaxed (alpha<1) sweeps ONLY once a period-2 limit cycle is actually detected — instead of unconditionally after k_full=6 sweeps — recovers H35's connectome gain without the -0.0019 pp microns loss, making it a clean 3-dataset GENERAL WIN.
items.rationale: findings.md #5 documents the exact cause: microns is capped at 12 sweeps, so k_full=6 leaves only 6 under-relaxed sweeps, not enough to overtake 12 full Jacobi sweeps. Detection (candidate score alternating between two values / mover set oscillating) is cheap and removes the hand-tuned constant.
items.kill_condition: If cycle-triggered alpha does not restore microns to >= H30's 83.2069 while holding connectome >= 83.9101.
items.est_cost: cheap (a detector plus a branch inside an existing refiner)

items.title: Gauss-Seidel / block-sequential exact-gain sift
items.hypothesis: Replacing the simultaneous (Jacobi) rebuild with sequential (Gauss-Seidel) or block-sequential updates — each node re-inserted against the CURRENT order, not the stale one — converges where Jacobi limit-cycles and reaches a strictly better fixed point than under-relaxation.
items.rationale: Under-relaxation (H35) is the textbook cure for a Jacobi 2-cycle; Gauss-Seidel is the other one, and usually the stronger. The open question is cost: the current kernel is vectorized-NumPy over all nodes at once, so a naive GS loses the vectorization. Block-sequential (K blocks, Jacobi within a block, sequential across blocks) is the practical middle and is a tunable interpolation between the two.
items.kill_condition: If block-sequential at any block count fails to beat H35 on the connectome prototype, or if the per-sweep cost exceeds the runtime budget.
items.est_cost: medium (needs a blocked kernel to keep vectorization)

items.title: Alternating discrete <-> continuous refinement with a frozen scale (A-ALT)
items.hypothesis: Alternating sift and a SHORT gradient phase whose position scale is pinned above the Q01 crossover (std >> 459) escapes the sift's fixed point, whereas a naive re-Rocket phase (std ~141) destroys it.
items.rationale: Q01 established that the surrogate only ranks a better order higher above std ~459, and that the optimum is HOLDABLE at its own scale. That is a concrete, testable prescription for the one place a gradient phase can still help. dr_tmp/kick_gate.py already scaffolds this probe with scales {150, 500, 1500} straddling the crossover — an unfinished experiment worth completing first.
items.kill_condition: If no scale above the crossover produces a post-re-sift gain over the sift fixed point, the hybrid direction is closed and Q01's prediction is confirmed in the strong form.
items.est_cost: cheap-medium (the scaffold exists; one connectome run per scale)
items.expected_pp: connectome 0 to +0.2; high information value either way

items.title: Structure-aware destroy operator for ruin-and-recreate (revives H31 under its stated condition)
items.hypothesis: A destroy operator that removes a CYCLE-DENSE or SCC-coherent set of nodes (rather than a random contiguous span) and re-inserts them by exact gain beats the plain sift, where H31's random ruin-and-recreate did not.
items.rationale: killed.json H31 revival condition names exactly this. The feedback weight is concentrated in the giant SCC; random destruction mostly re-does work the full-range sift already did.
items.kill_condition: No gain over the champion sift on the prototype proxy at <= 1.5x wall.

items.title: Segment / block moves instead of single-node re-insertion
items.hypothesis: Moving contiguous SEGMENTS (or coherent groups) of nodes as a unit reaches orders that no sequence of single-node insertions can, because the Rocket<->best difference is a distributed long-range reordering rather than a set of independent misplacements.
items.rationale: The gap structure (diagnosis Step 2) is a distributed reordering with Kendall-tau 0.61 and rank-distance p50 ~22,580 — consistent with whole regions being in the wrong place. Single-node exact-gain insertion is, by construction, blind to a move that is only profitable jointly.
items.kill_condition: If segment moves add nothing over the node sift on the hard synthetic (which is built to carry a verified gap), the move-class story is dead.

items.title: PHASE-2 SIZING (speed): how much Rocket does the pipeline actually need?
items.hypothesis: Because the discrete sift does most of the work and 'sift-on-greedy ~ sift-on-Rocket' was already observed, the 20k-epoch Rocket phase can be cut by an order of magnitude (or removed) at equal final score — a ~10x wall-clock reduction.
items.rationale: findings.md Phase-6 cross-cutting insight says the refiner does the work and the basin barely matters. If true, the expensive gradient phase is largely ceremonial. This is the single highest-leverage speed hypothesis and it is cheap to size: run the champion pipeline with epochs in {0, 500, 2000, 5000, 20000} and plot final score.
items.kill_condition: If final score degrades beyond the noise floor below 20k epochs, the gradient phase is load-bearing and Phase 2 must look elsewhere.
items.est_cost: cheap (5 connectome runs, no new code)
items.note: Sizing may run during Phase 1 (it is cheap and informative); any CHANGE to the champion pipeline waits for Phase 2.

items.title: Literature scan: post-2024 FAS / linear-arrangement / connectome-ordering methods
items.goal: Read Vahidi 2025 (arXiv:2506.13799) in full and extract its exact insertion/SCC mechanics; then sweep for newer FAS heuristics, and for adjacent literature (rank aggregation, minimum linear arrangement, DAG learning, topological ordering under noise) that carries transferable move classes.
items.output: autoresearch/lit/<date>-<topic>.md with concrete, falsifiable transfer ideas appended to this queue.
